newsitem.title: USA: Whirlpool says results will be lower.
newsitem.headline: Whirlpool says results will be lower.

text.p: Whirlpool Corp. said Friday it expects its third-quarter results, excluding restructuring charges, to be down 35 to 40 percent from a year earlier because of losses in Europe.
The company has also lowered its expectations for the full year.
Whirlpool said it will take a $30 million restructuring charge in the third quarter for the previously announced streamlining of its Asian headquarters and a North American refrigeration operation.

The maker of major home appliances said its less-favourable outlook for the third quarter was caused primarily by conditions in Europe, its second-largest market, where a continued difficult economic and industry environment is contributing to a lack of improvement in margins.
While third-quarter results will be significantly better than those for the second quarter, the situation will lead to a small quarterly operating loss at Whirlpool Europe.
Whirlpool reported an operating loss in Europe in the second quarter. It earned the equivalent of 70 cents a share in the second quarter.

However, North American profits rose nearly 70 percent in the second quarter, and Whirlpool Chairman David Whitwam said year-to-date results from the company's North American and Latin American operations are at record levels. He added that both regions are expected to perform strongly through the remainder of the year.
Whirlpool said it expects to report its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.
The company's stock, which did not trade early Friday, ended Thursday at $52.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
